newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil firm and tight.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil firm and tight.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil prices were firm on Wednesday amid tight supply, traders said.

High sulphur barges changed hands at $113 fob ARA in the morning but a combination of firmer crude and good bunker demand pushed prices higher by the afternoon, traders said. Barges also traded at $114 and $115 fob ARA, then at $116 fob Antwerp.
A 500 tonne low sulphur barge was traded at $126.50 fob ARA and dealers said the region was very tight.
An ARA player was heard having bought a cargo of M-100 fuel oil -- on the vessel 'Blue Star' -- from a refinery player at $113.50 cif NWE.
The same buyer was heard having bought another M-100 on Tuesday at $111. Another trader was heard offering another, similar cargo, at around $2 over the mean/mean of quotes.
A French refiner bought a high sulphur cracked cargo from a Scandinavian dealer on Tuesday at around quotes fob hi +$3.
Another refiner was thought to have bought another high sulphur cargo from another trader at a floating price.
Low sulphur markets were tight and quiet. A trader was heard buying a French-origin cargo at $124.50 fob NWE. This compares with October swaps deals at $125.50.
